title: Silent Letters in Words
keyIdea: A silent letter is written in a word but not said, like the k in knot, the w in wrap, the b in lamb and the t in listen. Silent letters often sit in the same pairs: k or g before n (knit, gnat, sign), w before r (wrist) and b after m (comb, climb). Many were said in Old English and dropped out of speech, but stayed in the spelling. Others were added later to show where a word came from, like the b in doubt, from the Latin dubitare. A related word where the letter is said can remind you to write it: sign and signal, muscle and muscular, autumn and autumnal.
familyTip: Go on a silent-letter hunt in a book or around the kitchen (knife, comb, wrap). For each find, say the word in a funny 'spelling voice' that sounds the silent letter, like k-nife. Then try to think of a relative where the letter is really said, such as bomb and bombard.

visual.caption: Where is the silent letter? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap the silent letter, sort kn, wr, gn and mb words, hear it in a relative, drag it back, fix the slip.

kid: Some words have a letter you write but do not say. It is called a silent letter. Knot sounds like not, but it starts with a k.
Silent letters like to sit in the same pairs. A k or a g can hide before n, as in knit and gnat. A w can hide before r, as in wrist. A b can hide after m, as in comb.
Long ago, people said many of these letters. The way we talk changed, but the spelling stayed the same.
A family word can help you. You do not hear the g in sign, but you do hear it in signal. So you know sign has a g.
adult: Ages 9 to 10. The national curriculum in England (English Appendix 1, Years 5 and 6) lists words with silent letters, such as doubt, island, lamb, solemn, thistle and knight. It says some of these letters were once sounded. This topic also asks pupils to use word families and word origins to remember the letter.

In Old English the k in knight and the w in write were said, and so was the b in lamb. The sounds dropped out of speech, but the spelling stayed. Other silent letters were never said in English. Scholars added the b in doubt to match the Latin dubitare, and the s in island came from a false link to isle. So a silent letter is not always a sound that was lost.

Common mistakes: spelling by sound alone (rite, thum, nife); putting the silent letter in the wrong place (kinfe); and treating an inflected form as a helpful relative. In signing the g is still silent, so only signal, signature or signify help. Watch for homophones too: knight and night, wrap and rap, and knot and not mean different things.

In the lab your child taps the silent letter in six words and sorts eight more into kn, wr, gn and mb families. They pick the relative that says the letter for six words, drag the letter back into six gaps, and find four slips.

practice.prompt: Which letter is silent in lamb?
practice.hint: Say lamb slowly. Which letter makes no sound?
practice.explain: lamb sounds like lam. The b after the m is silent.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters and one of them is silent. How many letters do you say?
practice.hint: Take away the one you do not say.
practice.explain: {n} letters minus 1 silent letter leaves {=n-1} letters you say, just as knot has 4 letters but you say 3.

practice.prompt: Which word helps you remember the c in muscle?
practice.hint: In which word can you hear a k sound?
practice.explain: In mus-cu-lar you say the c. muscles is the same word with -s, and mussel is a shellfish.

practice.prompt: A spelling list has {w} words. {s} of them have a silent letter. How many words have no silent letter?
practice.hint: Take the silent-letter words away from the whole list.
practice.explain: {w} words minus {s} with a silent letter leaves {=w-s} with none.

practice.hint: Think of the w before r family: wrap, wrist.
practice.explain: wrong starts with a silent w before the r.

pool.prompt: Which word has a silent k?
pool.hint: Find the k you write but do not say.
pool.explain: knee sounds like nee. You hear the k in kite and milk.

pool.prompt: I cut my ▢ on the tin. Which spelling is right?
pool.hint: Think of the b after m family: comb, lamb.
pool.explain: thumb has a silent b after the m.

pool.prompt: Which family does wrist belong to?
pool.hint: Look at the first two letters.
pool.explain: wrist starts with wr. The w before r is silent.

pool.prompt: Why is there a b in doubt?
choices: Writers added it to match the Latin dubitare.
It shows the word is a verb.
pool.hint: Think about where the word came from.
pool.explain: The b was never said in English. Scholars added it to show the Latin root, dubitare.

pool.prompt: A story has {k} words with kn and {m} words with mb. How many words with a silent letter is that?
pool.explain: {k} kn words and {m} mb words make {=k+m} words with a silent letter.

pool.prompt: Which word does NOT help you remember the g in sign?
pool.hint: In which word is the g still silent?
pool.explain: In signing the g is still silent. You hear it in signal and signature.

pool.prompt: The brave ▢ rode a horse. Which word fits?
pool.hint: A soldier, or the time when it is dark?
pool.explain: A soldier on a horse is a knight, with a silent k and gh. night is when it is dark.

pool.prompt: Which letter is silent in autumn?
pool.hint: Say it slowly, au-tum, and listen for the last letter.
pool.explain: The n is silent. You hear it in autumnal: au-tum-nal.

pool.prompt: You spell {n} silent-letter words. You forget the silent letter in {f} of them. How many did you spell right?
pool.hint: Take away the words that lost their letter.
pool.explain: {n} words minus {f} slips leaves {=n-f} spelt right.

pool.hint: Think of the t you do not say, as in castle.
pool.explain: listen has a silent t after the s, just like castle and whistle. lisen and lissen spell it by sound alone.
